January 3 35.

Dear Steptoe,

Further to my letter dated December 15,1934,

I have to inform you that Katherine Mayo and her husband
arrived in Shanghai on January 2, 1935, on board the S.S.
"Empress of Japan", having travelled from Vancouver B.C.
They gave the following particulars regarding themselves
on the Aliens' Passport Declaration Forms furnished by
the Chinese Authorities at the time of their disembarkation:-

Name.......... Katherine S.Mayo ......Paul Mayo
Age........... 33 ............40
Nationality.. American .......American
Place of Birth.Elkins, West .......Kansas
              Virginia.
Home address. Denver,Colorado. ......Denver, Colorado.
Passport..... American No.389625.....American No.149893
             issued by Dept.of State   issued by Dept.of State,
             Washington D.C. on May    Washington D.C. on Oct.
             25,1931. Renewed August   8,1934. Visa of Chinese
             18,1933. Visa of Chinese  Consulate-General, New
             Consulate-General,New     York, dated Oct.13,1934.
             York,dated 13-10-34.
Occupation... (None stated) ......Professor
Destination.. Peking ..........Peking
Object....... Travel ..........Travel
Length of stay..Few weeks ......Few weeks.

Accompanying the Mayos in a menial capacity is a
Miss Theresa Fanken.

After passing through the Chinese Maritime Customs,
Mr. and Mrs. Mayo made their way to the Cathay Hotel where
they are at present occupying Suite B.2 which was reserved
for them on January 1,1935 by a Mr. T.T. Bitting. The
latter resides at Room No.430 Cathay Hotel. Miss Franken
is staying in Room No.511 in the same hotel.

Yours sincerely,
〔此处为手写签名〕

H.H. Steptoe, Esq.

Dear Steptoe,

With reference to your letter dated

Special Branch - S.B.D. ____
REPORT
Date December 14, 1934

Subject (in full) Communication dated December 4, 1934 from U. S. Consulate-General relating to a contemplated visit to Shanghai of an American authoress named Katherine MAYO and her husband.
Made by D. S. Pitts, Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕

Acting on instructions received I have to state
that Dr. Liu, Chief of the Bureau of Public Safety Passport
Examination Office, No. 38 Avenue Edward VII, was confident-
ially approached on December 6, 1934 when he was asked if he
would be kind enough to inform Mr. Givens if and when an
American authoress named Katherine MAYO with her husband
arrived in Shanghai. Dr. Liu, who was informed that the
couple would probably be arriving from America, readily
assented to the request, and promised to let you know im-
mediately should the persons in question disembark here.
He also gave instructions for his subordinates to watch
carefully for the arrival of the Mayos.

All hotels and boarding houses are being watched
whilst the arrival lists of all steamers giving the names of
passengers are being closely scrutinised.

The source of the information contained in the
attached communication has not been divulged.

D. S. Pitts
D. S.

Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch).

1934年12月6日，秘密接触了位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）38号的公共安全局护照查验处处长刘博士（Dr. Liu），询问他是否愿意在名为凯瑟琳·梅奥（Katherine MAYO）的美国女作家及其丈夫抵达上海时通知吉文斯（Givens）先生。刘博士得知这对夫妇可能从美国抵达后，欣然同意了这一请求，并承诺一旦相关人员在此下船，将立即通知你。他还指示其下属密切关注梅奥夫妇的抵达情况。

所有酒店和寄宿公寓均处于监控之下，同时正在仔细审查列出乘客姓名的所有轮船抵达名单。

附件通讯中所含信息的来源尚未泄露。

D. S. 皮茨（D. S. Pitts）

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 289. SHANGHAI.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
4th December 1934
No. D 63111
Date 4 / 12 / 34

PERSONAL AND SECRET.

My dear Givens,

You are doubtless aware that the American
authoress Katherine Mayo made herself very unpopular among
Hindus by writing the book entitled "Mother India". I under-
stand that she and her husband are contemplating a visit
to China and Japan and that they have been granted in the
United States of America a British Empire wide visa on
their passports.

It is possible, therefore, that they may
attempt to go on to India from the Far East, though I hope
she will not do so as it will be very much against Mrs.
Mayo's own interest to make this journey. Would you be
good enough to ask the Chinese Passport Control Authorities
to let you know should Katherine Mayo and her husband arrive
here. Further, if you should hear that she purposes to
visit India, would you let me know.

Yours Sincerely,
Hartleyne

T. P. Givens Esq.,

（左侧批注：）
So,
For
attention
please in a
very discreet
way.
J.B.
pages.zh:
英国驻上海总领事馆，
邮政信箱 289. 上海。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. B. 登记处。
1934年12月4日
编号 D 63111
日期 1934年12月4日

私人且机密。

亲爱的吉文斯（Givens）：

你无疑知道，美国女作家凯瑟琳·梅奥（Katherine Mayo）因撰写题为《印度之母》（"Mother India"）一书而在印度教徒中极不受欢迎。据我了解，她和她的丈夫正计划访问中国和日本，并且他们的护照在美国获得了涵盖整个大英帝国的签证。

因此，他们有可能试图从远东继续前往印度，尽管我希望她不要这样做，因为这次旅行将对梅奥夫人自身的利益非常不利。能否请你要求中国护照管制当局在凯瑟琳·梅奥及其丈夫抵达此处时通知你。此外，如果你听说她打算访问印度，请告知我。

此致，
哈特利恩（Hartleyne）

T. P. 吉文斯（T. P. Givens）先生，

（左侧批注：）
所以，
请
以非常
谨慎的
方式
关注。
J.B.
